text: My office is in the sky! I check the weather before every flight, and I talk to the control tower. Last week, I flew from Jeddah to Kuala Lumpur.

speaker: DAD
text: I design buildings and bridges. I use a computer to draw plans, and I visit building sites to check the work. Safety is the most important part of my job.

speaker: MS_GREEN
text: My patients can't tell me where it hurts! I take care of cats, dogs, horses and sometimes camels. Yesterday, I helped a cat with a broken leg.

speaker: MR_HASSAN
text: Good morning, boys. Welcome to Career Day! Our first visitor is Mr. Turki. He's a software engineer.

speaker: MAN
text: Thank you. I make apps for phones. My team is making an app that helps farmers know when to water their plants. To do my job, you need to be good at math, and you need to love solving problems.

speaker: YUSUF
text: How many hours do you work every day?

speaker: MAN
text: About eight hours. But I can work from home two days a week.

speaker: MR_HASSAN
text: Thank you, Mr. Turki. Our second visitor is Captain Nasser. He's a firefighter.

speaker: DAD
text: Hello, everyone! Being a firefighter isn't only about fires. We also help people in car accidents and floods. We train every day to stay strong and fast.

speaker: DAD
text: Sometimes. That's why teamwork is so important. We always work together and look after each other.

speaker: SAMI
text: How can we stay safe at home?

speaker: DAD
text: Great question! Never play with matches, and make sure your home has a smoke alarm. And remember the emergency number: nine nine eight.

speaker: MS_GREEN
text: Right, class, our topic today is plans. Ben, what are you going to do this summer?

speaker: BEN
text: I'm going to visit my grandma in London. We're going to stay for three weeks. And I'm going to see the Science Museum again!

speaker: MS_GREEN
text: Lovely. And what about the future? What are you going to be?

speaker: BEN
text: I'm going to be a marine biologist, because I love the sea. I'm going to study the coral reefs in the Red Sea.

speaker: YUSUF
text: This summer, I'm going to take a computer course. I'm going to learn how to make games. In the future, I'm going to start my own game company!

speaker: SAMI
text: I'm not going to travel this summer. I'm going to help my grandpa on his farm and learn about plants. In the future, I'm going to be a doctor, like my dad.

speaker: MS_GREEN
text: Wonderful plans, boys. Remember: big dreams need hard work!

speaker: LINA
text: Noor, what does your uncle do?

speaker: NOOR
text: He's a journalist. He writes news stories for a newspaper in Jeddah.

speaker: LINA
text: Wow! Does he enjoy his job?

speaker: NOOR
text: Yes, he loves it. He meets interesting people every day. What about your aunt?

speaker: LINA
text: She's a judge. She works in a big building in the city.

speaker: NOOR
text: That sounds like a serious job!

speaker: LINA
text: It is. She has to read lots of documents. But she's very fair and kind.

speaker: NOOR
text: I'd like a job like that one day.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: I'd like a job like that.

speaker: YUSUF
text: Sami, what are you going to be when you grow up?

speaker: SAMI
text: I'm going to be a doctor. I want to help people.

speaker: YUSUF
text: That's a great career. You'll need to study for many years.

speaker: YUSUF
text: I'm going to be an engineer. I'm going to build the tallest tower in the world, here in Saudi Arabia!

speaker: SAMI
text: Ha ha! That's a big dream. Where are you going to study?

speaker: YUSUF
text: Maybe at a university in Riyadh, or maybe abroad. I'm not sure yet.

speaker: SAMI
text: Well, good luck! Let's meet here in twenty years and see!

speaker: NARRATOR
text: What are you going to be?

speaker: BEN
text: Good morning, everyone. My presentation is about four inventions that changed the world.

speaker: BEN
text: The first invention is paper. It was invented in China about two thousand years ago. Before paper, people wrote on stone, wood and animal skins.

speaker: BEN
text: The second is the printing press. A German man called Gutenberg made it in about fourteen forty. Books became cheaper, and more people learned to read.

speaker: BEN
text: The third is the telephone. In eighteen seventy-six, Alexander Graham Bell made the first phone call. He said, "Come here, I want to see you."

speaker: BEN
text: The last invention is the internet. It started in the nineteen sixties, but most people only started using it in the nineteen nineties. Today, more than five billion people use it!

speaker: BEN
text: Which invention is the most important? I think it's paper, because without paper, people couldn't share ideas for hundreds of years. What do you think?

speaker: MS_GREEN
text: Today, we're talking about staying safe online. The internet is amazing, but we need to be careful. Here are my top tips.

speaker: MS_GREEN
text: Tip number one: never share your password, not even with your best friend. Only your parents should know it.

speaker: MS_GREEN
text: Tip number two: don't share personal information, like your address, your school or your phone number, with people you don't know.

speaker: BEN
text: What if someone sends me a mean message?

speaker: MS_GREEN
text: Good question, Ben. Don't answer it. Take a screenshot and show it to a parent or a teacher. That's tip number three.

speaker: MS_GREEN
text: Tip number four: think before you post. Once a photo is online, it's very difficult to delete it forever.

speaker: ADAM
text: How long should we use screens every day?

speaker: MS_GREEN
text: Many doctors say children your age should spend no more than two hours a day on screens for fun. So, tip number five: take breaks, go outside and play!

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: Welcome to the final of the Young Inventors Robot Competition! Ten school teams built robots that help people in everyday life.

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: Our next team is from Taif: Sami and Yusuf. Tell us about your robot.

speaker: YUSUF
text: Our robot is called Sahm. It helps elderly people take their medicine on time.

speaker: SAMI
text: Sahm has a small screen and a speaker. At medicine time, it says, "It's time for your medicine," and it opens the right box.

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: Brilliant! How long did it take to build?

speaker: YUSUF
text: Three months. We worked on it every Tuesday and Thursday after school.

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: What was the most difficult part?

speaker: SAMI
text: The voice. At first, it was too quiet, so we changed the speaker. Now it's loud and clear.

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: And who gave you the idea?

speaker: YUSUF
text: Sami's grandpa! He sometimes forgets his medicine, so we wanted to help him.

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: What a kind idea. The judges will announce the winners at four o'clock. Good luck!

speaker: GRANDPA
text: Sami, can you help me with this new tablet? How does it work?

speaker: SAMI
text: Sure, Grandpa. First, press this button on the top to turn it on.

speaker: SAMI
text: Next, touch the picture of the camera. Then you can make a video call.

speaker: GRANDPA
text: Like this? Oh, I can see Noor!

speaker: SAMI
text: Yes! When you finish, touch the red button to stop the call.

speaker: GRANDPA
text: That's so simple. Thank you, Sami. You're a good teacher!

speaker: SAMI
text: You're welcome, Grandpa. Call me if you have any problems.

speaker: BEN
text: Adam, what do you think about tablets in class?

speaker: ADAM
text: I think they're really useful. We can find information quickly.

speaker: BEN
text: I agree, but in my opinion, books are better for reading long stories.

speaker: ADAM
text: That's a good point. But tablets are lighter than ten books in your bag!

speaker: BEN
text: Ha ha, that's true! What about robots in schools?

speaker: ADAM
text: Hmm, I don't think robots can be good teachers. A teacher understands how we feel.

speaker: BEN
text: I agree with you. Robots can help, but people are more important.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: I think it's a good idea.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: We should use it at school.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Tablets are good for learning English.

speaker: WOMAN
text: Welcome to Young Travelers. I'm here with three students who love traveling. Noor, which countries have you been to?

speaker: NOOR
text: I've been to Egypt, Malaysia and Japan. Japan was my favorite. I've never seen such clean streets! And I've tried sushi — it was delicious.

speaker: WOMAN
text: Wonderful. Ben, have you ever been somewhere really cold?

speaker: BEN
text: Yes, I have! I've been to Norway with my family. We saw the Northern Lights. The sky was green and purple. It was the most amazing thing I've ever seen.

speaker: YUSUF
text: I haven't traveled abroad yet, but I've visited many places in Saudi Arabia. I've climbed Jabal Sawda, the highest mountain in the Kingdom, and I've camped in the Empty Quarter.

speaker: WOMAN
text: That's impressive! Is there anywhere you haven't been but really want to visit?

speaker: YUSUF
text: Yes. I've always wanted to see the pyramids in Egypt.

speaker: NOOR
text: Oh, you must go! I've been there twice.

speaker: MAN
text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Diriyah. My name is Abdullah, and I'm your guide today.

speaker: MAN
text: Diriyah is very important in our history. It was the first capital of the Saudi state, which started almost three hundred years ago, in seventeen twenty-seven.

speaker: MAN
text: We're standing in At-Turaif, the old district. In twenty ten, UNESCO made it a World Heritage Site.

speaker: MAN
text: Look at the buildings. They're made of mud bricks, which keep the houses cool in summer and warm in winter.

speaker: MAN
text: The tour takes about ninety minutes. First, we'll visit Salwa Palace. Then we'll walk to the museum, where you can see old weapons and coins.

speaker: MAN
text: Please stay with the group, and don't climb on the old walls. They're very old and easy to damage.

speaker: MAN
text: At the end of the tour, there's traditional coffee and dates at the visitor center. Any questions?

speaker: BEN
text: Can we take photos inside the palace?

speaker: MAN
text: Yes, you can, but please don't use the flash.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Some places are so amazing that people call them "wonders of the world". Let's visit three of them.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Our first wonder is the Great Wall of China. With all its parts, it's more than twenty-one thousand kilometers long. It took about two thousand years to build, and millions of workers helped.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Our second wonder is the Great Pyramid of Giza, in Egypt. It was built about four thousand five hundred years ago. It was one hundred and forty-six meters tall, and it was the tallest building in the world for almost four thousand years! It has about two point three million stone blocks.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Our last wonder is Petra, in Jordan. The Nabataeans carved this city into pink rock about two thousand years ago. They were the same people who built Hegra, in AlUla.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Today, millions of tourists visit these places every year. That's why it's so important to protect them for the future.

speaker: ADAM
text: Ben, have you ever been to Abha?

speaker: BEN
text: Yes, I have. I went there last summer with my family.

speaker: ADAM
text: Lucky you! Have you ever tried the cable car there?

speaker: BEN
text: Yes! It was a bit scary, but the view was incredible. Have you ever been on a plane?

speaker: ADAM
text: No, I haven't. I've never flown anywhere. We always travel by car.

speaker: BEN
text: Really? You should try it one day. It's much faster.

speaker: ADAM
text: I'd love to. My dad says we're going to fly to Jeddah in the spring.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Yes, I have. I went there last ….

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You should try it one day.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Have you ever been to Abha?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Have you ever tried the cable car?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: I have been there three times.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: We have visited it with our family.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: She's never flown on a plane.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: I've always wanted to see the sea.

speaker: LINA
text: Noor, my cousin is visiting Saudi Arabia next month. Where should she go?

speaker: NOOR
text: She should definitely visit AlUla. It's amazing, especially at sunset.

speaker: NOOR
text: If she likes the sea, I'd recommend the Red Sea coast. The water is clear, and the fish are beautiful.

speaker: LINA
text: Great idea! And what's the best place to taste traditional food?

speaker: NOOR
text: Try a restaurant in old Jeddah — Al-Balad. The food is delicious, and the old buildings are wonderful.

speaker: LINA
text: Thanks, Noor. I'll send her your recommendations today.

speaker: NOOR
text: Tell her not to wait! Winter is the best time to visit.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: … is the best time to visit.

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: Good evening, and welcome to the final of the Taif Schools Football Cup! It's the Falcons against the Eagles, and the stadium is full tonight.

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: Twenty minutes into the game, and the Falcons have the ball. Yusuf passes to Sami... Sami shoots... Oh, it hits the post! So close!

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: Thirty-five minutes now, and the Eagles are attacking. Their captain, Omar, runs past two players... and scores! The Eagles lead one-nil.

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: It's half-time. The Falcons look tired, and their coach is not happy.

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: The second half has started, and what a change! The Falcons are playing much faster now. Adam crosses the ball... Ben jumps... and heads it in! Goal! It's one-all!

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: Only two minutes left. The crowd is on its feet. Sami has the ball again... he dribbles past the goalkeeper... and scores! The Falcons are winning two-one!

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: And there's the final whistle! The Falcons are the champions!

speaker: MAN
text: Okay, team, listen carefully. Tomorrow's tournament is the most important event of the year, so here's my advice.

speaker: MAN
text: First, sleep early tonight. Your body needs at least nine hours of sleep to recover.

speaker: MAN
text: Second, eat a good breakfast — eggs, bread and fruit — but don't eat a big meal just before the game. You'll feel heavy and slow.

speaker: MAN
text: Third, drink water all day. In this hot weather, you can lose more than a liter of water in one game.

speaker: MAN
text: During the game, keep talking to each other. Call your teammate's name before you pass the ball. Good teams communicate.

speaker: MAN
text: And remember: if we lose a point, don't argue with the referee. Stay calm and focus on the next play.

speaker: ADAM
text: What time should we arrive, Coach?

speaker: MAN
text: Be at the sports hall at eight o'clock. The first game starts at nine, against Al-Faisal School.

speaker: BEN
text: What if we lose the first game?

speaker: MAN
text: Then we learn from it and play better in the next one. Winning is great, but teamwork is what makes us champions.

speaker: MR_HASSAN
text: Today, we're choosing our class sports captain. Three students want the job. Listen to their speeches, and then you'll vote.

speaker: ADAM
text: Hello, everyone. I've played football for five years, and I know a lot about the game. As captain, I'll make sure we train hard every week. I believe that practice is the key to winning.

speaker: YUSUF
text: Hi, everyone. I'm not the best player in our class, but I'm a good listener. A captain needs to understand every player, not only the strongest ones. If you choose me, I'll make sure everyone gets a chance to play.

speaker: BEN
text: Hello! I think a captain should be positive. When we lose, I'll be the first to say, "Don't worry, we'll do better next time." I also have a plan: I want to organize a match against the teachers at the end of the year!

speaker: MR_HASSAN
text: Thank you, boys. Now, please write your choice on a piece of paper and put it in the box.

speaker: SAMI
text: I think football is the best sport in the world. Do you agree?

speaker: BEN
text: I see your point, but I don't agree. I think basketball is more exciting. There are more goals — sorry, more points!

speaker: SAMI
text: Ha ha! Maybe, but football is more popular. Billions of people watch the World Cup.

speaker: BEN
text: That's true. But popular doesn't always mean better.

speaker: BEN
text: I agree with you there — tennis is boring to watch.

speaker: SAMI
text: Really? I think it's okay, but I won't argue about it!

speaker: BEN
text: Ha ha. Let's agree that all sports are good for us!

speaker: MAN
text: Okay, Yusuf. You're the new referee for the school volleyball match. Are you ready?

speaker: YUSUF
text: I think so, Coach. What do I need to do?

speaker: MAN
text: First, make sure both teams have six players on the court.

speaker: MAN
text: Blow the whistle to start every point. And don't forget to count the points out loud.

speaker: YUSUF
text: What if a player touches the net?

speaker: MAN
text: Then the other team gets the point. And remember, be fair to both teams, even if your friends are playing.

speaker: YUSUF
text: Of course. Can I use a card if a player is rude?

speaker: MAN
text: Yes, you can. But try to stay calm and explain the rules first.

speaker: YUSUF
text: Thanks, Coach. I'll do my best!

speaker: YUSUF
text: Good morning, and welcome to the School Radio News. I'm Yusuf.

speaker: ADAM
text: And I'm Adam. Here are today's top stories.

speaker: YUSUF
text: Our first story: the school library has opened a new reading corner. It has more than five hundred new books in English and Arabic, and some comfortable bean bags. It's open every day during break.

speaker: ADAM
text: In sports news, our basketball team won the city tournament last Thursday. They beat Al-Faisal School by forty-two points to thirty-eight. Congratulations, team!

speaker: YUSUF
text: Next, an important message from the school nurse. Because the weather is getting hotter, please bring a water bottle to school every day. There are water fountains on every floor.

speaker: ADAM
text: And finally, some exciting news: Grade 6 students are planting fifty trees in the school garden next week. If you'd like to help, please sign up with Mr. Hassan before Sunday.

speaker: YUSUF
text: That's all for today. Have a great day!

speaker: WOMAN
text: Good evening. Here's the weather forecast for the weekend.

speaker: WOMAN
text: A cold wind from the north will bring cooler temperatures to most of the Kingdom. In Tabuk, temperatures will drop to five degrees at night, and there may be snow on the mountains of Jabal Al-Lawz.

speaker: WOMAN
text: In Riyadh, it will be sunny but cool, with a high of nineteen degrees. Strong winds in the afternoon will cause dust, so drivers should be careful.

speaker: WOMAN
text: On the west coast, Jeddah will be warm and humid, with a high of twenty-nine degrees. The sea will be rough on Saturday, so swimming isn't a good idea.

speaker: WOMAN
text: In the south, Abha and Al-Baha will have heavy rain on Friday afternoon. There may be flooding in some valleys, so please stay away from them.

speaker: WOMAN
text: Next week, the weather will be warmer again everywhere. Have a lovely weekend!

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: Are you curious about the world? Do you love asking "How?" and "Why?" Then don't miss the Taif Young Scientists Fair!

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: This year's fair is on the fourteenth and fifteenth of March, at the King Fahd Cultural Center. Entry is free for all students.

speaker: NOOR
text: I went last year, and it was the best day ever! I made my own slime and learned why it's sticky.

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: There will be more than eighty projects from schools all over the city, plus live science shows every hour.

speaker: SAMI
text: The robot show is amazing. You have to see it!

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: Visit the space zone and try our virtual reality rocket ride — it's the most exciting ride in town!

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: Doors open at four p.m. and close at ten p.m. Bring your family and your questions!

speaker: ANNOUNCER
text: The Taif Young Scientists Fair: where curious minds come alive!

speaker: BEN
text: Did you hear the news about our school?

speaker: BEN
text: Yesterday, the principal announced that our school won the national reading competition!

speaker: ADAM
text: Really? That's fantastic! Which students took part?

speaker: BEN
text: Twenty students from Grade 6. They read more than three hundred books in two months.

speaker: ADAM
text: Wow! Did they get a prize?

speaker: BEN
text: Yes, they did. According to Mr. Hassan, the school received ten thousand riyals for the library.

speaker: ADAM
text: That's great news. I'm going to read more books this term!

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Did you hear the news about …?

speaker: NOOR
text: Lina, look at this advert. It says, "Sparkle toothpaste is the best toothpaste in the world."

speaker: LINA
text: Hmm, that's not a fact. That's an opinion.

speaker: LINA
text: Because nobody can prove that it's the best. A fact is something you can check, like "It costs twelve riyals."

speaker: NOOR
text: I see. So "Our photographer took this photo in Jeddah" is a fact?

speaker: LINA
text: Yes, if it's true! But "It's the most beautiful photo ever" is an opinion.

speaker: NOOR
text: That's interesting. I think I'll check adverts more carefully from now on.

speaker: LINA
text: Good idea. Don't believe everything you hear!

speaker: SAMI
text: Good morning. Our class started a recycling project three months ago, and today I'd like to share our results.

speaker: SAMI
text: First, we put three bins in every classroom: blue for paper, yellow for plastic and green for food waste.

speaker: SAMI
text: Then, every Thursday, two students collected the bins and weighed the rubbish. At the beginning, we only recycled about five kilograms a week.

speaker: SAMI
text: After we made posters and talked in the morning assembly, things changed. By the third month, we were recycling more than twenty kilograms a week!

speaker: SAMI
text: We also used the food waste to make compost for the school garden. Our tomatoes have never been bigger!

speaker: SAMI
text: The biggest problem was plastic bottles. Many students still throw them in the wrong bin. So next term, we're going to put a special bottle bin next to the canteen.

speaker: SAMI
text: Remember: if every student recycles one bottle a day, our school can save more than ten thousand bottles a year. Thank you!

speaker: WOMAN
text: Hello, everyone. I work for the National Water Company. Did you know that Saudi Arabia is one of the driest countries in the world? We have no rivers that flow all year.

speaker: WOMAN
text: Much of our drinking water comes from the sea. We take the salt out in big desalination plants, and that uses a lot of energy and money.

speaker: WOMAN
text: That's why every drop counts. Here are some easy ways to save water.

speaker: WOMAN
text: Turn off the tap while you brush your teeth. This can save up to twelve liters every time!

speaker: WOMAN
text: Take a short shower instead of a bath. A five-minute shower uses about forty liters, but a bath can use more than one hundred.

speaker: WOMAN
text: Fix dripping taps. One dripping tap can waste more than fifteen liters a day.

speaker: WOMAN
text: And when you make wudu, use only the water you need. The Prophet, peace be upon him, taught us not to waste water, even at a flowing river.

speaker: BEN
text: How much water does one person use in a day here?

speaker: WOMAN
text: On average, more than two hundred and fifty liters. That's higher than in many countries, so we can all do better.

speaker: ADAM
text: Hi, Sami! Are you free on Saturday morning?

speaker: ADAM
text: There's a tree-planting event in Al-Hada. It's part of the Saudi Green Initiative. They want to plant ten billion trees across the country!

speaker: SAMI
text: Ten billion? That's incredible! How many trees are we planting on Saturday?

speaker: ADAM
text: About five hundred. Volunteers are working in groups of four, and each group plants about twenty trees.

speaker: ADAM
text: Wear old clothes and a hat, and bring gloves. They'll give us the tools and water. Oh, and bring sunscreen — there isn't much shade.

speaker: ADAM
text: At seven o'clock, before it gets hot. My dad can drive us. We'll pick you up at half past six.

speaker: SAMI
text: That's early, but okay! I'm sure my grandpa will want to come too. He loves trees.

speaker: YUSUF
text: What do you think our city will be like in twenty years?

speaker: SAMI
text: I think there'll be more trees. The Green Initiative will make Taif greener.

speaker: YUSUF
text: I hope so! Do you think we'll have flying cars?

speaker: SAMI
text: Maybe. But I don't think they'll be cheap. Most people will still drive normal cars — electric ones.

speaker: YUSUF
text: Electric cars will help the air, too. What about schools?

speaker: SAMI
text: I think students will learn with robots and virtual reality. But we'll still need teachers!

speaker: YUSUF
text: Definitely. And I'll probably be an engineer by then.

speaker: SAMI
text: And I'll be your doctor if you work too hard!

speaker: NARRATOR
text: What do you think … will be like?

speaker: LINA
text: Noor, our class needs to choose a project for Environment Week. Any ideas?

speaker: NOOR
text: I think we should stop using plastic bags in the school shop. If we sell cloth bags, we can reduce plastic a lot.

speaker: LINA
text: That's a good idea, but cloth bags cost more money.

speaker: NOOR
text: True, but they last for years. And if we decorate them, students will want to buy them!

speaker: LINA
text: You've persuaded me! What about the price?

speaker: NOOR
text: We could sell them for ten riyals each. It's a fair price, and the money can buy more trees for the garden.

speaker: LINA
text: Perfect. Let's present the idea to the class tomorrow.

speaker: MOM
text: Welcome to the planetarium! Sit back, look up, and let's travel through our solar system.

speaker: MOM
text: At the center is the Sun. It's a star, and it's so big that more than one million Earths could fit inside it!

speaker: MOM
text: The closest planet to the Sun is Mercury. It's the smallest planet, and one year there lasts only eighty-eight days.

speaker: MOM
text: Our home, Earth, is the third planet. It's the only planet we know with liquid water on its surface and living things.

speaker: MOM
text: Mars is called the Red Planet because its soil contains iron, which looks like rust. Scientists hope that humans will travel to Mars one day.

speaker: MOM
text: Jupiter is the largest planet. It has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot, and that storm is bigger than Earth!

speaker: MOM
text: Saturn is famous for its beautiful rings, which are made of ice and rock.

speaker: MOM
text: Great question! Uranus and Neptune are the coldest. They can be colder than minus two hundred degrees.

speaker: MAN
text: Today, we're going to make a simple volcano to see a chemical reaction. Please put on your safety glasses first.

speaker: MAN
text: Step one: put the small plastic bottle in the middle of the tray. The tray will catch the "lava".

speaker: MAN
text: Step two: pour two spoons of baking soda into the bottle. Use the funnel, so you don't make a mess.

speaker: MAN
text: Step three: add a few drops of red food coloring and a little dish soap. The soap will make more bubbles.

speaker: MAN
text: Step four — and this is the exciting part — slowly pour half a cup of vinegar into the bottle, then step back quickly!

speaker: YUSUF
text: Wow! It's coming out! Why does it happen?

speaker: MAN
text: When vinegar and baking soda mix, they make a gas called carbon dioxide. The gas needs space, so it pushes the liquid up and out of the bottle.

speaker: YUSUF
text: Well, last spring, I was hiking with my family in the mountains near Abha. I always take my camera with me, because I love taking photos of animals.

speaker: YUSUF

speaker: YUSUF
text: At first, I wasn't sure it was important. But my dad said, "Let's send the photos to the university." Two weeks later, a professor called us. She was very excited!

speaker: YUSUF
text: Because nobody had recorded this kind of lizard in that area before. Now scientists are going to study it.

speaker: YUSUF
text: Honestly, I was shocked at first! Then I felt really proud. It showed me that you don't have to be an adult to help science.
